topic: Using Compile-Time Constants and Conditional Compilation for Debugging Control
explanation: In advanced C programming, controlling debugging and logging behavior without incurring runtime overhead is crucial. This is achieved by defining compile-time constants or macros that evaluate to false during production, allowing the compiler to optimize away debugging code. Such techniques leverage the compiler's ability to eliminate dead code paths, ensuring zero runtime cost for debug statements in production builds. This approach enhances performance and maintains clean, efficient code while providing flexible debugging mechanisms.
